sources.locator: "Tonghak Peasant Revolution", revision 1375257262, § lead and § Siege of Jeonju Fortress

explanation: The English article says the alarmed Joseon government asked the Qing dynasty for military intervention against the rebellion, that the Qing deployed 2,700 soldiers, and that Japan — angered that the Qing had not notified it beforehand as the Convention of Tientsin promised — started the First Sino-Japanese War. The account of the siege of Jeonju repeats it: on 3 May 1,500 Qing troops and 6,000 Japanese troops landed at Incheon the same day, and the Japanese question about the Convention of Tientsin "soon caused the First Sino-Japanese War".
